comment: Port map for netlists/ctle_sp.cir. The tool turns this into port
sources on the named nets, for both the .sp sweep and the .ac
characterisation the model is fitted from, so the two see the
z0 in = 50 ohm: the receiver input is terminated to 100 ohm
differential by RT1/RT2 in the deck, which 2 x 50 ohm ports match.
z0 out = RD = 1000 ohm: the output IS a 1 kohm load node. A 50 ohm
port there would load the node to 47.6 ohm and measure a circuit
nobody builds, 26.4 dB down on this one.
Differential references are 2*z0: 100 ohm in, 2000 ohm out.
bias natural: each port's DC is the net's own operating-point
voltage, so no DC current flows through its z0 and the sweep
linearises about the operating point work/ctle.cir has. Measured
on a source follower, a port written DC 0 instead moved the node
from 243.8 mV to 7.7 mV and S21 by 7.8 dB.

bands.name: equaliser
reason: The equalisation band: up to 300 MHz, where this deck's zero
and pole live and where the fitted model is expected to be
exact. Moved here from sparam_compare.BANDS unchanged.

bands.name: below_step_ceiling
reason: Up to 2.083 GHz, which is where ten of the model's own
integration steps make one period. A FIXED NUMBER, written
down once from a measured run and never re-derived from the
model under test: a bar whose band moves with the model it
judges can absorb any regression. The ceiling check reports
separately if a model's own ceiling drifts away from it.

bars_comment: Moved here from sparam_compare.BARS with no digit changed, and with
what each one was measured at when it was set:
equaliser          db 0.25          measured 0.0788 dB at 251 MHz, 3.2x
below_step_ceiling db 0.25          measured 0.0788 dB at 251 MHz, 3.2x
The margins are in line with the 3.85x the repository's existing
time-domain CTLE golden carries (0.038997 against a 0.15 threshold).
